In late June 2026, NN, Inc. announced a major expansion of its liquid cooling production for NVIDIA AI data center racks, adding 47 new machine centers in its Wuxi, China plant with 100% of this new capacity already pre-sold and tied to multi-year, multi-product awards.
This move effectively deepens NN's role in NVIDIA's Asia supply chain while repurposing legacy automotive capacity and targeting US$80–US$90 million of accretive new business in 2026.
We'll now examine how NN's fully pre-sold expansion of NVIDIA-related liquid cooling capacity could reshape the company's existing investment narrative.
We've uncovered the 10 dividend fortresses yielding 5%+ that don't just survive market storms, but thrive in them.
To own NN, I think you have to believe its pivot from slower automotive and industrial markets toward higher value data center content can meaningfully change the story, even while the company is still unprofitable and carries meaningful debt. The fully pre sold NVIDIA liquid cooling expansion directly reinforces the near term growth catalyst of new program ramp ups, but it does not remove the execution and balance sheet risks that remain front and center.
Among the recent developments, NN's removal from the Russell Microcap Value Index in late June 2026 stands out alongside this NVIDIA news. Index removal can affect trading liquidity and share price volatility at the same time management is leaning into capital intensive growth tied to AI racks, which could sharpen the contrast between improving commercial momentum and ongoing funding, refinancing, and execution risks as the data center opportunity scales.
Read the full narrative on NN (it's free!)
NN's narrative projects $485.5 million revenue and $47.9 million earnings by 2028.
Uncover how NN's forecasts yield a $5.75 fair value , a 60% upside to its current price.
Yet while some analysts were already assuming NN could lift revenue to about US$489.5 million and earnings to roughly US$48.3 million by 2028, others will focus on how concentrated customer exposure and trade frictions might look in light of a bigger NVIDIA centric footprint, reminding you that informed investors weigh several very different narratives before deciding what they believe.
Explore 2 other fair value estimates on NN - why the stock might be worth as much as 60% more than the current price!

Our free NN research report provides a comprehensive fundamental analysis summarized in a single visual - the Snowflake - making it easy to evaluate NN's overall financial health at a glance.

Rule the board, you must. Choose a side in Monopoly: Star Wars Heroes vs. Villains , the classic property-trading board game reimagined with legendary characters, locations and rivalries from across the Star Wars universe.
Play as iconic heroes or infamous villains — each with unique abilities — to assemble a team and experience cinematic moments while competing with family and friends across locations from every era of the saga. Every roll of the dice brings new opportunities to build an empire and claim victory.
GeForce NOW makes it easy to take the battle between the light and dark sides across nearly any device. Jump into a match on a low-powered PC, Mac, phone, TV, tablet or handheld device and keep the fun going across the galaxy.
The final days of the GeForce NOW Summer Sale are here. Before the savings disappear, gamers can save $35 on a 12-month Performance membership or $70 on a 12-month Ultimate membership — unlocking GeForce RTX-powered gaming in the cloud across devices they already own.
The Performance membership delivers smooth, high-quality gaming with RTX-powered servers, making it easy to jump into favorite titles across PCs, Macs, phones, handhelds and TVs.
The Ultimate membership takes cloud gaming to the max with RTX 4080‑ or 5080‑class performance. Experience cinematic visuals, ultralow latency and responsive gameplay powered by technologies like NVIDIA DLSS , ray tracing and NVIDIA Reflex — all without the cost of a new gaming rig.
One GeForce NOW member recently called the Summer Sale “ quite significant ” after realizing the savings were even larger than expected in their local currency. By locking in a year of Ultimate, they calculated their monthly cost dropped from roughly 29 CAD to 17 CAD – showcasing how GeForce NOW continues to help gamers around the world enjoy the games they love, wherever they choose to play.
Plus, check out this spreadsheet , made by a community member, featuring discounted games streaming on GeForce NOW and build out a bigger library at the best bargains during the Steam Summer Sale .

latest_judgement.reasons: Rung 2 is the best-supported estimate, but the FY2027 filing amount is not established. The strongest quantified evidence is a $6.3 billion CoreWeave capacity-purchase contract and a later $3.5 billion addition for customer data-center lease guarantees. Together they indicate a scale near $10 billion, but they do not establish the aggregate amount that will be disclosed in the FY2027 filing. The newly announced cloud-provider program and reported provider plans lean toward greater exposure, but no amount is given, so they do not warrant moving to rung 3.

latest_judgement.reasons: The report of negotiations modestly favors a guarantee being announced by the deadline. It is only a rumour about negotiations, however—not evidence that NVIDIA has signed or announced a guarantee—so the Yes outcome is not established. The deadline is still in the future, and the evidence does not establish No either; rung 1 is the better-supported forecast, not a confirmed outcome.

evidence.quote: NVIDIA is providing financial guarantees to young cloud service providers that lease or rent its GPUs—if these companies fail to secure enough AI developers to rent their computing capacity, NVIDIA will repurchase their unsold GPU capacity at a pre-agreed price.
evidence.one_line: The Information reported on 2026-07-01 that NVIDIA guarantees young GPU cloud providers by agreeing to repurchase unsold capacity at a pre-agreed price if they cannot secure enough renters.
evidence.speaker: The Information, as reported by moomoo.com

evidence.quote: To date, NVIDIA has invested several billion dollars in equity stakes in multiple emerging cloud service providers and, in certain cases, agreed to lease back chips from these companies—including CoreWeave and Lambda—in transactions totaling several billion dollars.
evidence.one_line: moomoo.com reported that NVIDIA had invested several billion dollars in equity stakes in emerging cloud providers and entered chip leaseback transactions totaling several billion dollars, including with CoreWeave and Lambda.
evidence.speaker: moomoo.com

evidence.quote: In September 2024, NVIDIA committed to purchasing all of CoreWeave’s unsold capacity through 2032 if CoreWeave failed to secure tenants, under a contract then valued at $6.3 billion.
evidence.one_line: In September 2024, NVIDIA committed to purchase CoreWeave’s unsold capacity through 2032 if it failed to secure tenants; the contract was then valued at $6.3 billion.
evidence.speaker: moomoo.com, recounting NVIDIA’s commitment

evidence.quote: According to a regulatory filing submitted by NVIDIA in May of this year (covering the quarter ended in April), NVIDIA subsequently added another $3.5 billion to guarantee customer data center leases in exchange for rights to purchase their shares.
evidence.one_line: NVIDIA’s May 2026 regulatory filing, covering the quarter ended in April, reported an additional $3.5 billion to guarantee customer data-center leases in exchange for rights to purchase their shares.
evidence.speaker: NVIDIA, in a regulatory filing as reported by moomoo.com

evidence.quote: In return, NVIDIA will receive a percentage of these cloud providers’ revenue, with the revenue-sharing rate gradually declining over the term of the contract.
evidence.one_line: The Information reported on 2026-07-01 that NVIDIA will receive a share of participating cloud providers’ revenue, with the rate declining over each contract term.
evidence.speaker: The Information, as reported by moomoo.com

evidence.quote: GPU cloud providers Firmus and Sharon AI have already joined the program, and three executives with existing business ties to NVIDIA confirmed the arrangement.
evidence.one_line: The Information reported on 2026-07-01 that Firmus and Sharon AI had joined NVIDIA’s program and that three executives with NVIDIA business ties confirmed the arrangement.
evidence.speaker: The Information, as reported by moomoo.com

evidence.quote: On July 1, NVIDIA published a statement on its official website announcing a new business model that combines revenue sharing with credit support, enabling AI cloud providers to procure NVIDIA infrastructure without bearing the full upfront capital expenditure, and allowing them to offer computing services to downstream AI-native enterprises, model developers, and corporate clients.
evidence.one_line: On 2026-07-01, NVIDIA announced a business model combining revenue sharing and credit support for AI cloud providers procuring NVIDIA infrastructure.
evidence.speaker: NVIDIA

evidence.quote: According to the report, the initiative is internally referred to by some NVIDIA personnel as the 'AI Compute Partnership.' A NVIDIA spokesperson also confirmed the existence of the program.
evidence.one_line: A NVIDIA spokesperson confirmed the program’s existence; the report said some NVIDIA personnel internally call it the “AI Compute Partnership.”
evidence.speaker: NVIDIA spokesperson, as reported by moomoo.com

evidence.quote: According to NVIDIA’s official press release, the company will earn not only standard product revenue but also an additional share of cloud service revenue, creating a usage-based, recurring revenue stream.
evidence.one_line: NVIDIA said in its press release that the model will provide it an additional share of cloud-service revenue alongside standard product revenue.
evidence.speaker: NVIDIA

evidence.quote: NVIDIA positions this framework as the 'DSX AI Factory' model, targeting AI service scenarios requiring continuous cross-regional operations, high utilization rates, and multi-tenant accelerated computing.
evidence.one_line: NVIDIA described the framework as its “DSX AI Factory” model for continuous, cross-regional, multi-tenant accelerated computing services.
evidence.speaker: NVIDIA, as reported by moomoo.com

evidence.quote: Sharon AI and Firmus are the first cloud providers participating in this model.
evidence.one_line: NVIDIA’s model has Sharon AI and Firmus as its first participating cloud providers, according to the report published 2026-07-01.
evidence.speaker: moomoo.com

evidence.quote: Sharon AI plans to deploy up to 40,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs, while Firmus is constructing a DSX AI Factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, expected to scale up to 360 megawatts and accommodate up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs.
evidence.one_line: Sharon AI plans to deploy up to 40,000 GB300 GPUs; Firmus is constructing a Batam campus planned for up to 360 MW and 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs.
evidence.speaker: moomoo.com

evidence.quote: The company at the heart of the AI boom will help connect AI data centre operators with cloud service providers, simplifying the process for each side and establishing a new recurring "usagelinked earnings stream" for itself, chief financial officer Colette Kress wrote in a blog post on Wednesday.
evidence.one_line: Nvidia CFO Colette Kress said Nvidia would connect AI data centre operators with cloud service providers to simplify access and establish a recurring earnings stream; no amount or timeframe was specified.
evidence.speaker: Yahoo Finance article, recounting a blog post

evidence.quote: Under the company's branding of DSX AI factories, an aspiring AI start-up can access the cloud compute resources of a provider like Firmus Technologies with greater speed and flexibility than would otherwise be the case, Kress said.
evidence.one_line: Colette Kress said start-ups could access cloud compute from providers such as Firmus Technologies through Nvidia's DSX AI factories; no deployment amount or timeframe was specified.
evidence.speaker: Yahoo Finance article, recounting Kress's remarks

evidence.quote: According to prior reporting by The Information, NVIDIA has also recently been negotiating to provide financial guarantees for OpenAI’s lease of a large data center in Ohio—an asset that, if fully built out at current prices for chips, labor, power, and other materials, could cost as much as $500 billion.
evidence.one_line: The Information previously reported that NVIDIA was negotiating to guarantee OpenAI’s lease of an Ohio data center, whose full build-out could cost up to $500 billion.
evidence.speaker: The Information, as reported by moomoo.com
